title_en: Alfa Laval AB v. China National Intellectual Property Administration, Third Party: SWEP International AB — administrative dispute over invalidation of invention patent
ruling_gist_en: I. In the patent invalidation procedure, the amendment manner as a means should focus on achieving the legislative purpose that amendments to the claims must not exceed the scope disclosed in the original specification and claims and must not expand the scope of protection of the original patent—the two legal standards—while taking into account the efficiency of administrative review and the fair protection of the patentee's contributions. Overly strict restrictions on specific amendment manners should be avoided; otherwise, restrictions on amendment manners would become purely a punishment for the patentee's improper drafting of claims.

full_text_en:
Alfa Laval Corporate AB v. the China National Intellectual Property Administration and Third Party SWEP International AB — Administrative Dispute over Invalidation of Invention Patent Right

[Ruling Summary]

I. In patent invalidation proceedings, the method of amendment serves as a means and should focus on achieving the legislative purpose of satisfying the two major legal standards, namely that the amendment to the claims must not exceed the scope of the original description and claims and must not expand the scope of protection of the original patent, while taking into account the efficiency of administrative review and the equitable protection of the patentee's contributions. It is inappropriate to impose overly strict restrictions on the specific methods of amendment; otherwise, such restrictions on the method of amendment would become a pure punishment for the patentee's improper drafting of the claims.

II. When an amendment to a claim involves incorporating all or part of the additional technical features of a dependent claim into the independent claim from which it depends, the determination of whether the amended independent claim expands the scope of protection of the original patent shall be based on the scope of protection of the independent claim of the original patent that is the subject of the amendment.

Administrative Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2019) Zui Gao Fa Zhi Xing Zhong No. 19

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Alfa Laval Corporate AB. Domicile: Box 73, Lund, Kingdom of Sweden.

Legal Representative: Flip van Friesendorff, Group Patent Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Ke Ke, patent agent of China Patent Agent (H.K.) Ltd.

Agent ad litem: Peng Chang, patent agent of China Patent Agent (H.K.) Ltd.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): China National Intellectual Property Administration. Domicile: No. 9, West Fourth Ring North Road, Haidian District, Beijing, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Shen Changyu, Director General of the Administration.

Agent ad litem: Li Hui, Examiner of the Administration.

Agent ad litem: Wang Xiao, Examiner of the Administration.

Third Party at First Instance: SWEP International AB. Domicile: P.O. Box 105, Landskrona, Kingdom of Sweden.

Legal Representative: Scott Alan Howard, General Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Yu Yichao, Attorney at Zhong Lun Law Firm (Guangzhou).

Agent ad litem: Wu Xiaoxu, Attorney at Zhong Lun Law Firm.

The appellant Alfa Laval Corporate AB (hereinafter "Alfa Laval") appealed to this Court against the administrative judgment rendered by the Beijing Intellectual Property Court on February 25, 2019, in case (2016) Jing 73 Xing Chu No. 5802, concerning the administrative dispute over the invalidation of invention patent rights with the respondent China National Intellectual Property Administration (hereinafter "CNIPA") and the third party at first instance SWEP International AB. After this Court accepted the case on May 15, 2019, it lawfully formed a collegial panel and conducted an inquiry into this case on August 6, 2019. Ke Ke, agent ad litem for the appellant Alfa Laval, Wang Xiao, agent ad litem for the respondent CNIPA, and Yu Yichao and Wu Xiaoxu, agents ad litem for the third party at first instance SWEP International AB, appeared before the court for the inquiry. This case is now concluded.

Alfa Laval's appeal requests: to set aside the original judgment, to set aside the Invalidation Request Review Decision No. 29765 (hereinafter "the Decision under Review") made by CNIPA, and to order CNIPA to render a new invalidation request review decision. The relevant facts and reasons are as follows: (I) The original judgment and the Decision under Review erred in finding that the amended claims of the invention patent entitled "Method for Brazing Stainless Steel Products and Stainless Steel Brazed Products Obtained by the Method" (patent No. 200680018368.4, hereinafter "the patent-in-suit") expanded the scope of protection of the original patent. 1. Alfa Laval's amendment to the claims was by way of deleting a parallel technical solution and should have been accepted. (1) In patent invalidation administrative proceedings, the methods of amending claims are not limited to the three methods specified in the 2010 Patent Examination Guidelines; the Guidelines do not entirely exclude the possibility of other amendment methods. The amended claims constitute a further limitation on the authorized claim 1, and the amendment method should have been accepted. (2) The 2017 Patent Examination Guidelines amended the methods for amending claims in invalidation proceedings. According to the Guidelines, methods of amending claims include deletion of claims, deletion of technical solutions, further limitation of claims, and correction of obvious errors. In this case, the amended claim 1 can be regarded as incorporating the technical features of authorized claims 2 and 20 into claim 1 to narrow the scope of protection, which constitutes a further limitation on the claim and should have been accepted. 2. Alfa Laval's amendment to claim 1 did not expand the scope of protection of the original patent. In authorized claim 19, "containing ... at least one of 0-25 wt% Si, 0-6 wt% B, 0-15 wt% P, 0-8 wt% Mn, 0-2 wt% C, and 0-15 wt% Hf" should be interpreted as "at least one of the six elements: 0-25 wt% Si, 0-6 wt% B, 0-15 wt% P, 0-8 wt% Mn, 0-2 wt% C, 0-15 wt% Hf", and should not be interpreted as the original judgment's reading that "when these four elements are included, the content of each element must comply with the numerical limits". (1) In claim 20, when "0-25% Si" and "0-6 wt% B" are satisfied, the requirement of "at least one" is met. In such a case, even if it contains 16 wt% P, it is still consistent with the wording of the claim. That is, in claim 20, when it contains P, Mn, C, Hf, the amounts thereof are not limited to "0-15 wt% P", "0-8 wt% Mn", "0-2 wt% C", "0-15 wt% Hf". The interpretation that "when these four elements are included, the content of each element must comply with the numerical limits" cannot be derived from the literal meaning. (2) The description and drawings may be used to interpret the content of the claims. Paragraph [0047] of the specification of the patent-in-suit records the brazing filler metal composition and contents that the patentee intended to disclose, which discloses "at least 40 wt% Fe, 14-21 wt% Cr, 5-21 wt% Ni, 6-15 wt% Si, 0.2-1.5 wt% B, and the balance of other elements as substitutes." It can be seen that the specification clearly records a brazing filler metal containing certain amounts of Fe, Cr, Ni, Si, B, and other elements may or may not be present; when present, the contents are not limited. The above content indicates that the specification does not require that when the four elements P, Mn, C, and Hf are all present, the content of each element must comply with the numerical limits. (3) The administrative judgment of the Supreme People's Court (2014) Xing Ti Zi No. 17 established the principle of broadest reasonable interpretation for claim construction, i.e., based on the literal wording of the claims and combined with an understanding of the specification, to give the broadest reasonable interpretation to the claims. This principle should be followed in this case. In summary, the amendment method for the patent-in-suit should have been accepted, and the amended claims did not expand the scope of protection of the original patent. (II) The original judgment and the Decision under Review erred in finding that the claims were not supported by the description. According to authorized claim 1, the technical problem it solves is to provide a product with an average brazing area hardness of less than 600 HV1, and the examples further verify that authorized claim 1 can provide such a product. Although the specification of the patent-in-suit describes multiple technical problems, this does not mean that authorized claim 1 must solve all of them. As long as the claim solves one technical problem, such as providing a product with an average brazing area hardness of less than 600 HV1, it should be deemed to be supported by the description. When authorized claim 1 can solve the above technical problem, the other claims dependent on claim 1 can also solve the above technical problem, and thus are also supported by the description.

CNIPA argued in its defense: The original court found the facts clearly, applied the law correctly, and the procedure was lawful. It requested the dismissal of Alfa Laval's appeal. The relevant facts and reasons are as follows: (I) The original judgment correctly found that the amendment to the claims of the patent-in-suit expanded the scope of protection of the original patent. The amended claim 1 submitted by Alfa Laval during the invalidation proceeding did not include the features of authorized claims 18 and 19, and adopted an open-ended drafting style, which did not exclude that the iron-based brazing filler metal could contain the four elements P, Mn, C, and Hf. When the iron-based brazing filler metal contains the above four elements, since the amended claim 1 has no limitation thereon, it actually expands the scope of protection of the original patent. (II) The Decision under Review was made in 2016 and should not be subject to the relevant provisions of the 2017 Patent Examination Guidelines. Furthermore, according to Article 68 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China (revised in 2002) (hereinafter "the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law"), regardless of whether the 2010 or 2017 Patent Examination Guidelines apply, the above amendment should not be accepted. (III) The original judgment's finding that claim 1 was not supported by the description is affirmed. The specification of the patent-in-suit does not provide any rule or principle on the influence of the brazing filler metal composition, brazing temperature, and time on the hardness of the brazed area. A person of ordinary skill in the art, based on all the content disclosed in the specification, cannot determine whether technical solutions other than the specific point values of the brazing filler metal disclosed in the specific embodiments of the specification can achieve the limited hardness of the brazed joint.

SWEP International AB argued in its defense: The original court found the facts clearly, applied the law correctly, and the procedure was lawful. It requested the dismissal of Alfa Laval's appeal. The relevant facts and reasons are as follows: (I) Regarding the review basis. 1. From a literal interpretation, a person of ordinary skill in the art clearly understands the meaning of "at least one". When protecting two or more components, the content of the components claimed by "at least one" must satisfy the scope limited by the other components in the claim. The administrative judgment of the Supreme People's Court (2014) Xing Ti Zi No. 17 relied on by Alfa Laval mainly concerns the definition of the meaning of claim terms, which is different from the present case's interpretation of claim scope arising from the dependency relationship. It cannot be simply applied. 2. The scope of protection of the amended claim. When incorporating the features of authorized claims 2 and 20, Alfa Laval did not add all the additional technical features of claims 18 and 19, which materially affects the scope of protection of the claim. 3. According to the principle of non-retroactivity, the 2017 Patent Examination Guidelines do not apply to this case. (II) Regarding Article 26, Paragraph 4 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China (revised in 2001) (hereinafter "the Patent Law"). 1. The technical problem of the patent-in-suit. Based on the claims and the description of the patent-in-suit, the technical problem to be solved by the patent is to use an iron-based brazing filler metal to weld stainless steel products, ensuring the filling and sealing performance of large brazing gaps, thereby overcoming the problem of strength loss in the prior art when using copper-based or nickel-based brazing filler metals. The technical problem asserted by Alfa Laval is incorrect. 2. The patent-in-suit is not supported by the description. First, the findings of the Decision under Review and the original judgment on this issue are affirmed. Second, although the specification of the patent-in-suit contains literal descriptions of the relevant technical features of the claims, the specification does not record the effects and experimental data of such contents. The specification does not provide substantive support for the claims. The technical features are only consistent in form of expression with the specification. A person of ordinary skill in the art still cannot know whether these contents can solve the technical problem sought to be solved by the present invention.

Alfa Laval filed a lawsuit with the original court, which accepted the case on November 8, 2016. Alfa Laval requested in its complaint: to set aside the Decision under Review and to order CNIPA to render a new invalidation request review decision. The relevant facts and reasons are as follows: (I) Alfa Laval's amendment to claim 1 was by way of deleting a parallel technical solution and should have been accepted. According to the dependency relationship of the claims, authorized claim 20 includes two parallel technical solutions, i.e., the technical solution dependent on claim 1 and the technical solution dependent on claim 2. The technical solution of Alfa Laval's amended claim 1 is actually the technical solution of authorized claim 20 dependent on claim 2, deleting the technical solution of authorized claim 20 dependent on claim 1. This falls within the deletion of a parallel technical solution. The literal additional technical features of authorized claims 18 and 19 are already implied in authorized claim 20 and do not affect the scope of protection of the dependent claim 20. When authorized claim 20 contains P, Mn, C, or Hf, the amounts thereof are not limited to the amounts of these four elements limited by claim 19. Therefore, when drafting the technical solution of authorized claim 20 as an independent claim, the literal additional technical features of claims 18 and 19 may be omitted. In summary, the scope defined by the literal features of the amended claim 1 is exactly the scope defined by all features of one technical solution of authorized claim 20, and the amendment should have been accepted. (II) The amended claim 1 does not exceed the scope of the original application and does not expand the scope of protection of the patent, and should have been accepted. The methods of amending claims in invalidation proceedings are not limited to the three methods specified in the 2010 Patent Examination Guidelines. In this case, the original specification already describes an iron-based brazing filler metal containing at least 40 wt% Fe, 14-21 wt% Cr, 5-21 wt% Ni, 6-15 wt% Si, and 0.2-1.5 wt% B. The amended claim 1 does not exceed the scope of the original specification and narrows the scope of protection. Such an amendment should have been accepted. (III) The Decision under Review erred in determining the technical problem to be solved by claim 1, leading to an erroneous finding on whether claim 1 is supported by the description. Although the specification of the patent-in-suit describes multiple technical problems, this does not mean that claim 1 must solve all technical problems. As long as claim 1 can solve one of the technical problems, it should be deemed to be supported by the description. The technical problem to be solved by claim 1 is to provide a product with an average brazing area hardness of less than 600 HV1, and the specification of the patent-in-suit also describes this technical problem. Therefore, claim 1 is supported by the description. Other claims dependent on claim 1 also solve the same technical problem and are therefore supported by the description.

CNIPA argued in its defense at first instance: The Decision under Review found the facts clearly, applied the law correctly, the trial procedure was lawful, and the conclusion of the review was correct. Alfa Laval's grounds of action could not stand. (I) Alfa Laval's amended claim 1 during the invalidation proceeding did not include the features of authorized claims 18 and 19, which does not comply with Article 68 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law and the 2010 Patent Examination Guidelines. (II) Claim 1 was not supported by the description, in violation of Article 26, Paragraph 4 of the Patent Law. Therefore, it requested the dismissal of Alfa Laval's lawsuit.

SWEP International AB stated at first instance: The Decision under Review found the facts clearly, applied the law correctly, the trial procedure was lawful, and the conclusion of the review was correct. Alfa Laval's grounds of action could not stand. (I) Alfa Laval's amendment to the claims did not comply with the amendment rules of the 2010 Patent Examination Guidelines. (II) A person of ordinary skill in the art cannot determine whether other implementations besides the iron-based filler components disclosed in the specification can achieve a welded joint hardness of less than 600 HV1. (III) The evidence submitted by Alfa Laval during the litigation stage was not the basis on which CNIPA made the Decision under Review and should not be admitted. Therefore, it requested the dismissal of Alfa Laval's lawsuit.

The original court found the following facts: Alfa Laval is the patentee of the invention patent entitled "Method for Brazing Stainless Steel Products and Stainless Steel Brazed Products Obtained by the Method", patent No. 200680018368.4. The filing date of this patent is May 24, 2006, the priority date is May 26, 2005, and the grant and publication date is June 16, 2010. The contents of the authorized claims 1, 2, 18, 19, and 20 of the patent-in-suit are as follows:

"1. A method for brazing stainless steel products, comprising:

(i) applying an iron-based brazing filler material to a stainless steel component;

(ii) optionally assembling the components;

(iii) heating the component from step (i) or (ii) to at least 1000°C in a non-oxidizing atmosphere, a reducing atmosphere, a vacuum, or a combination thereof, and heating the component at a temperature of at least 1000°C for at least 15 minutes;

(iv) providing a resulting product having an average hardness of the brazed area of less than 600 HV1; and

(v) optionally repeating one or more of steps (i), (ii), and (iii).

2. The method of claim 1, wherein a joint, hole, gap, crack, or fissure greater than 76 μm is sealed or filled by the method.

18. The method of claim 1 or 2, wherein the iron-based brazing filler material contains one or more of Si, B, P, Mn, C, or Hf.

19. The method of claim 18, wherein the iron-based brazing filler material contains 9-30 wt% Cr, 5-25 wt% Ni, and at least one of 0-25 wt% Si, 0-6 wt% B, 0-15 wt% P, 0-8 wt% Mn, 0-2 wt% C, and 0-15 wt% Hf.

20. The method of claim 19, wherein the iron-based brazing filler material contains at least 40 wt% Fe, 14-21 wt% Cr, 5-21 wt% Ni, 6-15 wt% Si, and 0.2-1.5 wt% B."

In response to the invalidation request filed by SWEP International AB, Alfa Laval submitted an amended set of claims on July 21, 2014, which incorporated the additional technical features of dependent claims 2 and 20 into claim 1, deleted claims 18-22, and adjusted the dependency relationships. The amended claim 1 read as follows:

"1. A method for brazing stainless steel products, comprising:

(i) applying an iron-based brazing filler material to a stainless steel component, wherein the iron-based brazing filler material comprises at least 40 wt% Fe, 14-21 wt% Cr, 5-21 wt% Ni, 6-15 wt% Si, and 0.2-1.5 wt% B;

(ii) optionally assembling the components;

(iii) heating the component from step (i) or (ii) to at least 1000°C in a non-oxidizing atmosphere, a reducing atmosphere, a vacuum, or a combination thereof, and heating the component at a temperature of at least 1000°C for at least 15 minutes;

(iv) providing a product wherein the brazed region has an average hardness of less than 600 HV1; and

(v) optionally repeating one or more of steps (i), (ii), and (iii), wherein joints, holes, gaps, cracks or fissures larger than 76 μm are sealed or filled by the method.

On August 3, 2016, the National Intellectual Property Administration issued the decision under review. The decision found that: the amendment to the claims submitted by Alfa Laval Company on July 21, 2014 did not comply with Article 68 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law and Section 4.6.2 of Chapter 3, Part IV of the 2010 Patent Examination Guidelines; the technical solutions of granted claims 1, 19-22, 24, 28-32 were not supported by the specification, and the other claims could not overcome the above defects; therefore, the specification of the patent at issue did not comply with Article 26(4) of the Patent Law. Accordingly, the patent at issue was declared wholly invalid.

During the oral hearing in the invalidation proceeding, Alfa Laval Company stated that the realization of the technical problem to be solved by the patent at issue was related to content, and also related to temperature and time; the inventive point of the patent at issue was not merely substituting iron for copper.

During the first-instance proceedings, Alfa Laval Company submitted the Invalidation Request Review Decision No. 24591 issued by the National Intellectual Property Administration, to demonstrate that the National Intellectual Property Administration had previously recognized that the 2010 Patent Examination Guidelines did not completely exclude the possibility of other amendment methods, and that amendments not conforming to the methods prescribed in the 2010 Patent Examination Guidelines could be accepted.

At the first-instance court hearing, Alfa Laval Company clarified that its objection to the decision under review's assessment under Article 26(4) of the Patent Law was solely that the decision under review incorrectly identified the technical problem to be solved by claim 1 of the patent at issue, thereby leading to an erroneous conclusion as to whether the patent at issue complied with Article 26(4) of the Patent Law.

The court of first instance held:

(1) Regarding whether the amendment to the claims by Alfa Laval Company should be accepted. Alfa Laval Company amended the claims during the examination of the invalidation request, and the amended independent claim included all technical features of granted claim 1 and the additional technical features of claims 2 and 20. Alfa Laval Company stated that the technical solution of the amended claim 1 was in fact the technical solution of granted claim 20 when it referred to claim 2. However, granted claim 20 referred to claim 19, and claim 19 referred to claim 18. If Alfa Laval Company used the technical solution of granted claim 20 referring to claim 2 as the content of the amended independent claim, the amended independent claim should also include the additional technical features of granted claims 18 and 19. Granted claim 18 defined that the iron-based brazing filler material contained one or more of Si, B, P, Mn, C, or Hf. Granted claim 19 defined that the iron-based brazing filler material contained at least one of Cr, Ni, Si, B, P, Mn, C, Hf, and provided a range for the amount of each element, i.e., when the iron-based brazing filler material contained multiple of the above elements, the amount of each element should be limited by the numerical values recorded in claim 19. Although the amended claim 1 defined that the iron-based brazing filler material simultaneously contained five elements Fe, Cr, Ni, Si, B, and the content ranges of Cr, Ni, Si, B were all smaller than the content ranges recorded in the claims to which it referred, the amended claim 1 adopted an open-ended drafting method and did not exclude the possibility that the iron-based brazing filler material could contain the four elements P, Mn, C, Hf. When the iron-based brazing filler material contained these four elements, since the amended claim 1 placed no limit on the specific content ranges of these four elements, it actually expanded the scope of protection of the original patent, violating Article 68 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law.

(2) Regarding whether the patent at issue complied with Article 26(4) of the Patent Law. Providing a product wherein the brazed region has an average hardness of less than 600 HV1 was a step in the method of granted claim 1. On this basis, the decision under review found that the technical problem to be solved by the patent at issue was to use an iron-based brazing filler to weld stainless steel products, ensuring filling and sealing performance during the brazing of large gaps, thereby overcoming the defects in the prior art that copper-based brazing fillers were consumed due to corrosion and nickel-based brazing fillers lost strength in large-gap brazing. This finding was not improper. Furthermore, when the decision under review assessed whether the claims of the patent at issue were supported by the specification, it also assessed whether the method according to the claims of the patent at issue could necessarily achieve the specific hardness of the welded joint, i.e., for the technical problem that Alfa Laval Company argued in the litigation phase should be solved by the patent at issue, the decision under review had actually assessed it when evaluating whether the patent at issue complied with Article 26(4) of the Patent Law, which did not affect the final determination. The inventive point of the patent at issue was not merely substituting iron for copper; the realization of the technical problem to be solved by the patent at issue was related to content, and also related to temperature and time. Alfa Laval Company also acknowledged this during the oral hearing in the invalidation proceeding. However, the specification of the patent at issue did not provide the rules or principles regarding the influence of the composition ratio of the brazing filler, temperature, and time on the hardness of the welded region. Based on all the content disclosed in the specification, a person skilled in the art could not determine that technical solutions other than the embodiments disclosing specific values of the brazing filler in the detailed description of the specification could all solve the technical problem to be solved by the patent at issue. Therefore, the technical solution of claim 1 of the patent at issue was not supported by the specification. Claims 1-34 of the patent at issue all did not comply with Article 26(4) of the Patent Law.

In summary, the court of first instance rendered judgment: dismissing the claims of Alfa Laval Company. The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 100 was to be borne by Alfa Laval Company.

The facts found by the court of first instance were essentially correct, and this Court confirms them.

This Court further finds: Paragraph [0047] of the specification of the patent at issue states: According to another alternative aspect of the present method, the iron-based brazing filler material may comprise at least 40% by weight Fe, 14-21% Cr, 5-21% Ni, 6-15% Si, 0.2-1.5% B, and the balance of other elements as substitutes. According to another alternative aspect of the present method, the iron-based brazing filler material may comprise at least 40% by weight Fe, 14-21% Cr, 5-21% Ni, 4-9% Si, 4-9% P, and the balance of other elements as substitutes.

This Court holds that the issues in dispute in this appeal are: whether the amendment to the claims of the patent at issue by Alfa Laval Company should be accepted; and whether the patent at issue complies with Article 26(4) of the Patent Law.

(1) The issue as to whether the amendment to the claims of the patent at issue by Alfa Laval Company should be accepted

Article 68, paragraph 1, of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law provides: "During the examination of an invalidation request, the patentee of an invention or utility model patent may amend the claims, but shall not broaden the scope of protection of the original patent."

Words are tools for expressing thoughts. Once a patent document is fixed in written form, its technical solution is determined. However, both the accuracy of language expression and the cognitive ability of the patentee may have limitations, especially cognitive limitations regarding the prior art and the invention. Therefore, the Patent Law grants the patentee the right to amend the patent document. On one hand, to protect the patentee's invention and technical contribution, thereby promoting innovation incentives in society, the patentee should be allowed to make appropriate amendments to the patent document, and patent invalidation should not be simply used as a punishment for the patentee's inadequate drafting skills. On the other hand, although the patentee is allowed to make appropriate amendments to the patent document, during the invalidation proceeding, based on the public's reliance interest in the published patent document, it is necessary to prevent the patentee from using the amendment opportunity to supplement into the patent document technical content that was not completed at the time of patent application. Therefore, the patentee's amendment of claims is subject to certain restrictions, and it is specifically required that amendments to claims during the invalidation proceeding shall not go beyond the scope of protection of the original patent. This is an institutional design to balance the interests of the patentee and the public interest. Generally speaking, any amendment to the claims will change the scope of protection of the patent. To determine whether an amendment made by the patentee during the administrative invalidation proceeding should be accepted, the standards shall be that the amendment does not broaden the scope of protection of the original patent and does not go beyond the content recorded in the original specification and claims. In this regard, depending on the specific circumstances of the case, the content disclosed in the original patent document should be examined with moderate flexibility, and consideration should be given comprehensively in conjunction with the characteristics of different amendment methods.

In this case, to determine whether the amendment to the claims of the patent at issue by Alfa Laval Company should be accepted, it is necessary to make a specific determination based on the manner and content of the amendment to the claims.

1. Regarding the manner of amendment to the claims. The decision under review held that when granted claim 18 referred to claim 2, the technical solution of claim 20 should include all technical features of claims 1, 2, 18, 19, and 20, whereas the current amendment method only added the additional technical features of granted claim 20 to claim 1 or claim 2. Therefore, it found that the patentee's manner of amending the claims did not comply with Article 68 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law and the 2010 Patent Examination Guidelines. Analyzing the above review logic, the decision under review refused to accept the amendment on the ground that the manner of amendment to the claims of the patent at issue did not conform to the amendment methods prescribed in the 2010 Patent Examination Guidelines. In this regard, this Court holds that although the 2010 Patent Examination Guidelines relied upon by the decision under review provided that the manner of amending claims during the invalidation proceeding was generally limited to three methods: deletion of claims, combination of claims, and deletion of technical solutions, it did not completely exclude the possibility of other amendment methods. In the invalidation proceeding, the amendment method, as a means, should focus on achieving the legislative purpose of satisfying the two major legal standards that the amendment must not go beyond the scope of the original specification and claims and must not broaden the scope of protection of the original patent, while taking into account the efficiency of the administrative review and fairly protecting the patentee's contribution. It is not appropriate to impose overly strict restrictions on specific amendment methods; otherwise, the restriction on amendment methods would become purely a punishment for the patentee's improper claim drafting. In particular, the 2017 Patent Examination Guidelines extended the amendment methods in the invalidation proceeding to four basic methods, including deletion of claims, deletion of technical solutions, further limitation of claims, and correction of obvious errors. On the premise that the amendment to the claims satisfies the two major legal standards of not going beyond the scope of the original specification and claims and not broadening the scope of protection of the original patent, a moderate relaxation of the amendment methods not only helps the patent confirmation proceeding focus on the core of the invention, but also does not affect the public's reliance interest in the published patent document. In this case, the amendment method of Alfa Laval Company was to further limit the technical features of dependent claims 2 and 20 into granted claim 1, which constitutes a further limitation of the claim. This amendment method should be accepted.

2. Regarding the benchmark for comparing whether the amendment of claims does not broaden the scope of protection of the original patent. In a patent invalidation proceeding, when the amendment to claims consists of incorporating all or part of the additional technical features of a dependent claim into the independent claim to which it refers, to determine whether the amended independent claim broadens the scope of protection of the original patent, the benchmark for comparison should be the scope of protection of the independent claim of the original patent that is the subject of the amendment. That is, the amended independent claim should be compared with the independent claim having the broadest scope of protection in the original patent, not with a dependent claim having a narrower scope of protection. This is because after a patent is granted, it serves a public notice function to society, and the public's reliance interest is usually established on the independent claim with the broadest scope of protection, based on which they predict and evaluate the legality of their own actions. Incorporating the additional technical features of a dependent claim into the independent claim constitutes a further limitation of the independent claim, which does not broaden the scope of protection of the original independent claim but rather narrows it. On this basis, it will not impair the public notice effect of the original patent, nor will it harm the public's reliance interest based on the original patent. In this case, Alfa Laval Company amended the claims of the patent at issue during the invalidation proceeding by incorporating the additional technical features of dependent claims 2 and 20 into granted claim 1, which is a further limitation of granted claim 1 and does not broaden the scope of protection of granted claim 1. The court of first instance held that because the amended claim 1 placed no limit on the specific content ranges of the elements P, Mn, C, Hf in claim 19, it broadened the scope of protection of the original patent. The above finding effectively compared the amended claim with the scope of protection of claim 19 of the original patent, which was an erroneous benchmark. This Court corrects this error.

In summary, the manner in which Alfa Laval Company amended the claims during the invalidation proceeding should be accepted, and the scope of amendment did not exceed the scope of protection of the original patent; the amendment complied with Article 68 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law. The court of first instance erred in this finding, and this Court corrects it. Alfa Laval Company's appeal claim that the amended claim 1 did not exceed the scope of protection of the original patent is well-founded, and this Court supports it.

(2) The issue as to whether the patent at issue complies with Article 26(4) of the Patent Law

Article 26(4) of the Patent Law provides: "The claims shall be supported by the specification and shall define the scope of patent protection sought." Since the decision under review erroneously found that Alfa Laval Company's amendment to the claims during the invalidation proceeding broadened the scope of protection of the original patent, when determining whether the claims of the patent at issue complied with Article 26(4) of the Patent Law, it relied on the claims as granted. As discussed above, this Court holds that the amendment to the claims by Alfa Laval Company during the invalidation proceeding should be accepted. Therefore, this case needs to be reassessed on the basis of the amended claims to determine whether the patent at issue complies with Article 26(4) of the Patent Law. To avoid loss of the parties' right to appeal on the merits, the National Intellectual Property Administration shall make a new determination based on the patentee's amended claims.

In conclusion, Alfa Laval Company's appeal request is partially well-founded and should be supported. The judgment of the first instance contains errors in the application of law, and this Court corrects them. Pursuant to Article 26(4) of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China as revised in 2001, Article 68 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China as revised in 2002, and Articles 70, 89(1)(2) and (3) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. The administrative judgment (2016) Jing 73 Xing Chu No. 5802 of the Beijing Intellectual Property Court is reversed;

2. The Invalidation Request Review Decision No. 29765 of the National Intellectual Property Administration is reversed;

3. The National Intellectual Property Administration shall make a new review decision on the invalidation request filed by SWEP International Company against the invention patent titled "Method for Brazing Stainless Steel Products and Stainless Steel Brazed Products Obtained by the Method" with patent number 200680018368.4.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 100 and the second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 100 are both to be borne by the National Intellectual Property Administration.

This judgment is final.
